micro.copy: The living operator that keeps finite AI agents aligned to your venture's ability to continue.

short.copy: Cambium is the operator above your finite AI agents. It wakes on real events, checks the venture's viability, advances its current mission, routes one bounded specialist run, gates consequential actions, and records why the move happened—so the business can continue without hiding judgment from its founder.

medium.copy: Your agents can mint a brand, build a product, publish a campaign, and operate a workflow. Each one plays a finite game and should eventually stop. Cambium is the living layer between those runs. It carries the venture's vision, current mission, goals, limits, authority, and learning across time. When evidence arrives, Cambium wakes, checks margin to explicit viability bounds, and proposes one bounded next game. Reversible work can proceed within policy. Paid, irreversible, identity-changing, or externally representative actions stop at the founder gate. Every consequential decision lands with a replayable receipt before the operator returns to rest.

full.copy:
A business is not a project that reaches done. It is an infinite game that ends only when it loses the will or resources to continue. Yet most AI business systems are built from finite players: one mints a brand, one builds software, one publishes, one operates. Those bounded runs should finish. The problem is that nothing lives between them.

Cambium is that missing operator. It holds typed world-state for the venture, watches explicit viability bounds, regulates the vision-to-mission-to-goal cascade, and chooses which finite specialist game should happen next. It is dormant between events, but it never declares the venture finished.

Cambium does not maximize activity or revenue as a terminal objective. Revenue is fuel and solvency is a hard bound. Mission coherence, legal and ethical limits, and founder capacity are bounds too. The system uses observable proxy margins rather than pretending to compute an exact high-dimensional viability kernel.

When a real event arrives, Cambium checks source, freshness, and relevance; reads current margin; proposes a bounded move; applies the correct authority gate; persists the result; and returns to rest. Simulated founder and customer perspectives may propose. They never commit.

The outcome is not a company without a human. It is a company whose continuity no longer depends on constant human vigilance—and whose consequential choices remain legible to the real steward.

extended.copy:
The modern founder can summon a fleet of specialist agents, but the company still stops when the founder stops. Each agent is optimized for a bounded task: shape the brand, build the site, send the campaign, reconcile the queue. Those are finite games. They have clear briefs, stopping conditions, and artifacts. Finishing them is correct.

The failure appears between the games. No single specialist owns the venture's near-invariant vision, renewable mission, changing goals, legal boundaries, solvency floor, founder capacity, or accumulated learning. No one decides which finite game should happen next or whether the proposed move narrows the company's ability to continue. The founder remains the only continuity layer.

Cambium is the living operator above the finite system. Named for the tissue beneath bark that preserves old rings while making the next ring possible, Cambium holds typed, event-sourced world-state and wakes only when real evidence arrives. On each wake it evaluates explicit viability bounds and observable proxy margins. It asks whether the venture remains solvent, coherent with its mission, legally and ethically inside the field, and compatible with the founder's current capacity.

The operator then proposes one bounded next game. Reversible and pre-authorized work can proceed. A move that spends money, publishes externally, changes identity, moves sensitive data, or cannot be undone remains fail-closed until the designated human authority approves it. Simulated founder and ideal-customer agents may help explore a trajectory, but they cannot create commitment.

Every consequential step records the triggering event, evidence, prior state, authority, decision, output, and receipt. That makes the venture replayable: the founder can understand not only what happened, but why the system believed the move was viable.

Cambium does not promise guaranteed growth, an exact viability kernel, or a synthetic executive team. Revenue is treated as fuel and solvency as a bound, not as the purpose of play. The source objective is to advance the cause while preserving the ability to continue. The result is a different kind of autonomy: less constant supervision, more explicit limits, and human authority exactly where consequence begins.
